question: How do the five principles of prompting combine into an end-to-end AI blog-writing workflow in the user's own style?
contributions: A LangChain chain: SERP research and summaries, LLM-generated interview questions, outline, retrieval-backed section writing, style rewrite, title A/B test, image generation, Gradio UI.

results.claim: In the style-rewrite experiment, prompts were tested against three test cases scored by embedding distance (lower is closer to a hand-rewritten reference).

limits: Experiment is tiny: three test cases, no run count or spread stated in text, scores only in Fig 10-1.
Single-prompt baseline is criticised by checklist, not measured.
Evaluation advice is explicitly informal ('haphazard and messy').
Code uses pydantic.v1, LangChain 2023-24 APIs and Midjourney/SDXL; printed code has a retry-loop fallback that never writes the section.
practices: Audit a long prompt against the five principles (direction, format, examples, evaluation, division) (AI Blog Writing).
Do not rely on instructions that dictate a number of sections or words; models are bad at counting (Format).
Split the task into chained steps, each in LangChain for logging (AI Blog Writing).
Generate interview questions from research summaries to inject unique opinions (Expert Interview).
Use Pydantic output parsers so chain outputs are structured objects (Generate Outline).
Keep memory to AI messages only to avoid bloat from retrieved docs (Text Generation).
Ask for a writing-style guide without naming the author, ending with a bullet to fix the format (Writing Style).
Test prompts across multiple cases with 10 or more runs each (Writing Style).
A/B test titles with thumbs-up/down and compare score and token usage; try DSPy if quality is short (Title Optimization).
Name a style (e.g. Corporate Memphis) to steer image models; use meta-prompting to have one model write another's prompt (AI Blog Images).
Prototype the UI with Gradio or Streamlit before building a production frontend (User Interface).
Collect human feedback through the UI to find edge cases (User Interface).
